UnitSquares24

24 is the largest cycle on which every open position squares to 1
Proved in Leanring 1One wheel at a time: squares, characters and the number 24

On the cycle of a given length, call a position open when it shares no factor with the length. Every open position squares to 1 on the cycle exactly when the length divides 24. So every prime from 5 on squares to one more than a multiple of 24. In number-field language this says the number w₂ of the rational numbers is 24 (the largest cycle whose units all have order dividing 2, the Carmichael function dividing 2); it is the same 24 that appears in the Birch–Tate formula (node BirchTateRational). A classical fact, not new here.

Claims (2)

units_square_one_iff
proved in Lean
For a cycle length other than 0, every unit of the cycle squares to 1 exactly when the length divides 24.
/-- **Every open position squares to 1 exactly on the divisors of 24.** For a
cycle length `m` other than 0, every unit of the cycle squares to 1 if and
only if `m` divides 24. -/
def units_square_one_iff : Prop :=
  ∀ m : ℕ, m ≠ 0 → ((∀ u : (ZMod m)ˣ, u ^ 2 = 1) ↔ m ∣ 24)
Rests on: no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)
Statement in Conclusions.lean ↗
Proof: RNS.UnitSquares24.units_square_one_iff_holds ↗
prime_sq_mod_24
proved in Lean
Every prime from 5 on squares to one more than a multiple of 24.
/-- **Prime squares on the cycle of 24.** Every prime from 5 on squares to one
more than a multiple of 24. -/
def prime_sq_mod_24 : Prop :=
  ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → 5 ≤ p → p ^ 2 % 24 = 1
Rests on: UnitSquares24.units_square_one_iff
Statement in Conclusions.lean ↗
Proof: RNS.UnitSquares24.prime_sq_mod_24_step ↗
